Universal enveloping algebras and quantum groups

📄

Definition 4.10 ∀ stated (Quantum group \(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\)). \(\forall\) Let \(q\in\mathbb{C}^{*}\) with \(0<\lvert q\rvert\le 1\). The quantum group \(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\) is the associative \(\mathbb{C}\)-algebra generated by \(E,F,K,K^{-1}\) subject to

\[\begin{align} KK^{-1}&=K^{-1}K=1, \label{eq:quantum-KK}\\[3pt] KEK^{-1}&=q^2\,E,\quad KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}\,F, \label{eq:quantum-KE}\\[3pt] [E,F]&=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}. \label{eq:quantum-EF} \end{align}\]

In the classical limit \(q\to 1\), the generator \(K\) reduces to \(\exp(h\,e_3)\) and the relations recover the \(\mathfrak{su}(2)\) commutation relations.

📄

Proposition 4.11 ∀ stated (Yang–Baxter equation and braid operator from the \(R\)-matrix). \(\forall\)

The universal \(R\)-matrix \(\mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) \;\hat{\otimes}\; \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\) (quantum SU(2)) satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation

\[\mathcal{R}_{12}\,\mathcal{R}_{13}\,\mathcal{R}_{23} \;=\; \mathcal{R}_{23}\,\mathcal{R}_{13}\,\mathcal{R}_{12},\]

and the braid operator \(\check{R} = P \circ \mathcal{R}\) (where \(P\) is the tensor swap) furnishes a representation of the braid group on any tensor product of finite-dimensional \(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\)-modules, replacing the classical twist/flip involutions (braid twist-flip).

📄

Remark 4.12 ✗ no Lean (\(R\)-matrix and braiding).

The \(R\)-matrix of \(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\) (quantum SU(2)) is the universal element

\[\mathcal{R}\;\in\; \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\;\hat{\otimes}\; \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\]

satisfying the Yang–Baxter equation \(\mathcal{R}_{12}\mathcal{R}_{13}\mathcal{R}_{23} =\mathcal{R}_{23}\mathcal{R}_{13}\mathcal{R}_{12}\). Its action on a tensor product of representations gives the braid operator \(\check{R}=P\circ\mathcal{R}\) (where \(P\) is the swap), furnishing a \(q\)-deformed braid group representation that replaces the classical twist/flip involutions (braid twist-flip).

📄

Proposition 4.13 ∀ stated (Crossing asymmetry and per-crossing Coulomb correction). \(\forall\)

The Skein relation weights positive crossings by \(q\) and negative crossings by \(q^{-1}\):

\[q \, L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} L_- \;=\; (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})\, L_0.\]

For \(q > 1\), the per-crossing repulsive Coulomb correction relative to a mixed-charge baseline is

\[\delta_{\mathrm{Coulomb}} \;=\; q \;-\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1}) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \;>\; 0,\]

and the ratio of the antisymmetric (Coulomb) to symmetric (strong) Skein weights is

\[\frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}} \;=\; \tanh(\ln q).\]

At \(q = 1\) the asymmetry vanishes; at \(q \to \infty\) the ratio approaches \(1\).

📄

Remark 4.14 ✗ no Lean (Crossing asymmetry and emergent Coulomb repulsion).

The \(R\)-matrix braiding (R-matrix) introduces a fundamental asymmetry between positive and negative crossings: the Skein relation

\[q \, L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} L_- \;=\; (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})\, L_0\]

weights positive crossings by \(q\) and negative crossings by \(q^{-1}\). Since \(q > 1\), positive crossings contribute more to the Skein polynomial than negative ones. This asymmetry is the topological origin of electromagnetic repulsion.

Emergent Coulomb repulsion. For a hadron \(\mathfrak{H}\) with Coulomb charge \(Q(\mathfrak{H})\) (Coulomb charge), the crossing energy (crossing energy) decomposes into a symmetric (strong) baseline and an antisymmetric (Coulomb) correction. The per-crossing repulsive correction between composites of the same charge relative to a mixed-charge baseline is

\[\delta_{\mathrm{Coulomb}} \;=\; q \;-\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1}) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \;> 0.\]

Unification of strong and electromagnetic interactions. Electromagnetic repulsion is not a separate force in the QOU framework. It is a phase asymmetry in the same Skein polynomial that encodes the strong binding. Both interactions arise from the \(R\)-matrix braiding of \(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\), with \(q\) controlling the relative strength:

  • The strong binding is proportional to \(\tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1})\) (the baseline Skein weight).

  • The electromagnetic repulsion is proportional to \(\tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})\) (the crossing asymmetry).

Their ratio is

\[\frac{\text{Coulomb}}{\text{Strong}} \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}} \;=\; \tanh\!\left(\ln q\right).\]

At \(q = 1\) (classical limit), the asymmetry vanishes and the electromagnetic interaction disappears. At \(q \to \infty\) (deep-quantum regime), the ratio approaches \(1\) and the two interactions become comparable.

The specific assignment of Coulomb charges to protons and neutrons — and the consequences for nuclear stability — require the Descartes universe (\(\chi = -6\)) and are developed in Chapter 6.

Categorical Möbius energy and self-avoidance

📄

Proposition 4.15 ∀ stated (Categorical recovery of Möbius energy). \(\forall\)

Let \((\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)\) be a quantum observable universe (Definition) with substrate parameter \(q\) (Definition), categorical action \(\mathcal{S}_q\) (Definition), and \(q\)-Hodge star \(\star_q\) (Definition).

Let \(\varrho \colon S^1 \to \tau(A)\) be a smooth closed curve (a knot embedding) and let \(\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)\) denote the categorical mass (Theorem).

Define the categorical Möbius energy by

\[E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho) \;=\; \int_A \!\circ\, \mathrm{tr}_A \!\iint_{S^1 \times S^1 \setminus \mathrm{diag}} \!\!\Bigl( \Delta(\varrho(s)) \otimes \Delta(\varrho(t)) \Bigr) \;\star_q\; \Bigl\lVert \frac{d\varrho}{ds} \wedge_q \frac{d\varrho}{dt} \Bigr\rVert\, ds\, dt\,,\]

where \(\Delta\) is the Hopf comultiplication, \(\int_A\) is the Frobenius form (Remark), and the integration excludes the diagonal \(\mathrm{diag} \subset S^1 \times S^1\).

Then in the classical limit \(q \to 1\), the categorical Möbius energy recovers the classical Möbius energy up to a topological normalization:

\[\lim_{q \to 1}\; E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho) \;=\; \frac{1}{4}\, E(\varrho) \;+\; \text{const}\,.\]

Here \(E(\varrho)\) is the classical Möbius energy

\[E(\varrho) \;=\; \iint_{S^1 \times S^1} \Bigl( \frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2} \;-\; \frac{1}{D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t))^2} \Bigr) \lvert \varrho'(s) \rvert \, \lvert \varrho'(t) \rvert\, ds\, dt\,.\]

Here \(D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t))\) denotes the intrinsic arc-length distance along \(\varrho\).

Proof of Categorical recovery of Möbius energy. \(\forall\)

The proof proceeds in three steps.

Step 1: Gauge fixing via the categorical volume constraint. The categorical volume constraint fixes the gauge group to \(G = \mathrm{SU}(2)\), acting on the \(\mathbb{CP}^1\) fibre by Möbius transformations. This ensures that \(E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\gamma)\) is invariant under the full Möbius group \(\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})\), matching the conformal invariance of the classical functional.

Step 2: Expansion of the Frobenius–Hopf kernel. At \(q = 1\) the \(q\)-Hodge star reduces to the classical Hodge star, and the comultiplication \(\Delta\) becomes cocommutative. The Frobenius pairing \(\int_A \circ \mu\) on \(A \otimes A\) reduces to the standard \(\mathrm{SU}(2)\) Killing form, so the integrand simplifies to

\[\mathrm{tr}\bigl( \Delta(\gamma(s)) \otimes \Delta(\gamma(t)) \bigr) \;\xrightarrow{q \to 1}\; \frac{1}{\lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2}.\]

The repulsive kernel \(1/r^2\) is thus the classical shadow of the resistance of the Frobenius–Hopf object \(A\) to local deformations of the connection \(\nabla\): the Frobenius form \(\int_A\) assigns a diverging cost when two strands of \(\gamma\) approach.

Step 3: Subtraction of the self-energy. The diagonal regularization in the categorical integral (exclusion of \(\mathrm{diag} \subset S^1 \times S^1\)) matches the arc-length subtraction \(1/D(\gamma(s),\gamma(t))^2\) in the classical Möbius energy. In the \(q\)-deformed setting, this subtraction arises naturally from the antipode \(S\) of the Hopf structure: the self-pairing \(\int_A(\gamma(s)^* \cdot S(\gamma(s)))\) cancels the short-distance divergence at \(s = t\), leaving a finite integral that agrees with \(E(\gamma)/4\) up to an Euler characteristic correction \(\chi(\Sigma_\gamma) \cdot \mathrm{const}\), where \(\Sigma_\gamma\) is any Seifert surface spanning \(\gamma\). ◻

📄

Corollary 4.16 ∀ stated (Obstruction to self-intersection). \(\forall\)

Let \(\varrho\) be a knot embedding with categorical Möbius energy \(E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)\) as in Proposition, and let \(q \neq 1\) be the substrate parameter (Definition).

The non-cocommutativity of the Hopf structure at \(q \neq 1\) provides a categorical obstruction to self-intersection: the energy \(\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)\) diverges whenever two non-adjacent strands of \(\varrho\) approach within the fibre \(\tau(A)\).

Proof of Obstruction to self-intersection. \(\forall\)

The mechanism is as follows. The universal \(R\)-matrix \(\mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\) (Remark) controls the failure of the cocommutativity square

\[\sigma \circ \Delta \;\neq\; \Delta,\]

where \(\sigma\) is the tensor swap. At \(q = 1\) one has \(\mathcal{R} = 1 \otimes 1\) and the comultiplication is cocommutative, so strands may pass through each other freely (the "classical" regime where self-intersection is not penalised by the energy functional).

For \(q \neq 1\), the braiding \(\check{R} = \sigma \circ \mathcal{R}\) is non-trivial, and the categorical mass acquires a singular contribution from non-adjacent strand proximity. Concretely, because \(\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)\) depends on the \(q\)-Hodge star \(\star_q\) (Definition), the cost of two non-adjacent points \(\varrho(s)\), \(\varrho(t)\) approaching is governed by the \(q\)-deformed commutator

\[[\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q \;=\; \hat{X}\hat{P} - q\,\hat{P}\hat{X} \;=\; i\hbar_q,\]

which replaces the classical \(1/r^2\) repulsion kernel with the strictly stronger

\[\frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2} \;\longmapsto\; \frac{[2]_q}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2 - \hbar_q^{\,2}},\]

where \([2]_q = q + q^{-1}\) is the quantum integer and \(\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}\) is the quantum Planck constant. This kernel has a hard singularity at \(\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert = \hbar_q\), creating an energy barrier of infinite height at the quantum scale.

Physically, the \(R\)-matrix endows the vortex filament \(\varrho\) with a "quantum exclusion zone" of radius \(\hbar_q\): the filament cannot pass through itself because doing so would require infinite categorical energy. This is the knot-theoretic analogue of the Pauli exclusion principle, with the non-cocommutativity of \(\Delta_q\) playing the role of fermionic statistics. ◻

Crossing energy and Coulomb charge

📄

Definition 4.17 ∀ stated (Crossing energy of a knot composite). \(\forall\)

Let \(\mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \bowtie \mathcal{L}\) be a composite of knots linked by a link \(\mathcal{L}\), with braid word \(\beta \in B_n\) representing the linking. The crossing energy of \(\mathfrak{H}\) is

\[\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) \;=\; \sum_{\text{crossings in } \beta} \begin{cases} q & \text{positive crossing } (L_+), \\ -q^{-1} & \text{negative crossing } (L_-), \end{cases}\]

where \(q\) is the substrate parameter (substrate parameter) and the sign convention follows the Skein relation

\[q \, L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} L_- \;=\; (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})\, L_0.\]

The crossing energy measures the net Skein weight of the composite: positive \(\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}\) indicates repulsion dominates, negative indicates binding dominates. This quantity is computed entirely from the \(R\)-matrix braiding (R-matrix) of \(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\) acting on the tensor product of constituent representations.

📄

Definition 4.18 ∀ stated (Coulomb charge of a knot composite). \(\forall\)

Let \(\mathfrak{H}\) be a knot composite with braid word \(\beta\). Write \(n_+(\beta)\) and \(n_-(\beta)\) for the number of positive and negative crossings in \(\beta\). The Coulomb charge of \(\mathfrak{H}\) is

\[Q(\mathfrak{H}) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(n_+(\beta) - n_-(\beta)\bigr).\]

The crossing energy (crossing energy) decomposes as

\[\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) \;=\; \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)(q + q^{-1})}_{\text{baseline (strong)}} \;+\; \underbrace{Q(\mathfrak{H}) \cdot (q - q^{-1})}_{\text{Coulomb correction}}.\]

The first term is symmetric in \(q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}\) and represents the strong binding; the second is antisymmetric and vanishes at \(q = 1\). The Coulomb charge \(Q(\mathfrak{H})\) governs the magnitude and sign of the electromagnetic correction:

  • \(Q(\mathfrak{H}) > 0\): net positive crossings, repulsive Coulomb contribution.

  • \(Q(\mathfrak{H}) = 0\): electromagnetically neutral.

  • \(Q(\mathfrak{H}) < 0\): net negative crossings, attractive Coulomb contribution.

The ratio of Coulomb to strong contributions is \(\tanh(\ln q) \approx 0.104\) at \(q = q_0\).

Lagrange Resolvents and \(q\)-Deformed Kinematics

📄

Proposition 4.19 ∀ stated (Discrete Fourier transform diagonalises \(C_5\) on the Bring’s surface). \(\forall\)

Proposition. Let \(C_n\) act on a vector space \(V\) of dimension \(n\) with coordinates \(x_0, \ldots, x_{n-1}\), and let \(\zeta = e^{2\pi i/n}\). The Lagrange resolvent transform (discrete Fourier transform on \(C_n\)) is

\[w_k \;=\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\zeta^{kj}\,x_j, \qquad k \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\}.\]

Then:

  1. The cyclic permutation \(\sigma \colon x_j \mapsto x_{j+1}\) acts diagonally: \(\sigma(w_k) = \zeta^{-k} w_k\). The \(C_n\) symmetry is manifest as phase rotation of the Fourier modes.

  2. Any \(C_n\)-invariant polynomial constraint on the \(x_j\) transforms to a constraint on \(C_n\)-equivariant combinations of the \(w_k\) (products pairing \(w_k\) with \(w_{n-k}\), i.e.\{} conjugate modes).

For \(n = 5\) (the case relevant to Bring’s surface), the three power-sum constraints transform to: \(w_0 = 0\) (linear projection), \(w_1 w_4 + w_2 w_3 = 0\) (Hermitian quadric), and \(w_1^2 w_3 + w_4^2 w_2 + w_2^2 w_1 + w_3^2 w_4 = 0\) (symmetric cubic).

📄

Remark 4.20 ✗ no Lean (Lagrange resolvents and spectral form).

Let \(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/n}\). The discrete Fourier transform on \(C_n\) (Lagrange resolvent transform) diagonalises the cyclic action: \(\sigma(w_k) = \zeta^{-k} w_k\). Any \(C_n\)-invariant polynomial constraint on the coordinates \(x_j\) transforms to constraints on \(C_n\)-equivariant combinations of the Fourier modes \(w_k\).

For \(n = 5\) (Bring’s surface), the three power-sum equations become:

\[\begin{align} w_0 &= 0 &&\text{(linear projection),} \label{eq:resolvent-linear}\\[4pt] w_1\,w_4+w_2\,w_3 &= 0 &&\text{(Hermitian quadric),} \label{eq:resolvent-quadric}\\[4pt] w_1^2\,w_3+w_4^2\,w_2+w_2^2\,w_1+w_3^2\,w_4 &= 0 &&\text{(symmetric cubic).} \label{eq:resolvent-cubic} \end{align}\]

The quadric pairs conjugate modes (\(w_k\) with \(w_{5-k}\)); the cubic pairs squared modes in the skip-one pattern. These are the \(C_5\)-equivariant invariants \(h_2\) and \(h_3\) (aggregate color quantities).

📄

Definition 4.21 ∀ stated (\(q\)-Momentum from the braid writhe). \(\forall\)

The \(q\)-momentum of a particle is the writhe of its braid representative, weighted by the Hecke deformation parameter.

Definition. Let \(\beta \in B_n\) be a braid representative of a particle knot \(K = \hat{\beta}\) (braid closure), with generators \(\sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k}\) where \(\epsilon_j = \pm 1\). The \(q\)-momentum is:

\[p_q(\beta) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{k} \epsilon_j \, \frac{q^{\epsilon_j} - q^{-\epsilon_j}}{q - q^{-1}} \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{k} \frac{q^{2\epsilon_j} - 1}{q^2 - 1}\]

At \(q = 1\): \(p_q(\beta) \to w(\beta)\), the classical writhe (sum of crossing signs).

At the substrate parameter \(q\): each positive crossing contributes \([1]_q = 1\) and each negative crossing contributes \([-1]_q = -1\), but with \(q\)-weighting that distinguishes the two.

Equivalently, the \(q\)-momentum is the trace of the braid in the fundamental representation of \(H_n(q)\):

\[p_q(\beta) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{fund}}(\rho(\beta))\]

where \(\rho: B_n \to H_n(q)\) is the Hecke representation.

Properties.

  1. Additivity under concatenation: \(p_q(\beta_1 \beta_2) = p_q(\beta_1) + p_q(\beta_2)\) (from the trace being linear on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra).

  2. Invariance under Markov I: \(p_q\) is conjugation-invariant (cyclic property of the trace).

  3. Shift under Markov II: stabilization \(\beta \mapsto \beta \sigma_n^{\pm 1}\) shifts \(p_q\) by \(\pm [1]_q\). This is the \(q\)-analogue of adding one unit of momentum.

  4. Parity: Under the mirror \(\sigma: \beta \mapsto \beta^{\sigma}\) (reverse all crossings), \(p_q(\beta^{\sigma}) = -p_{q^{-1}}(\beta)\). Parity violation at \(q \neq 1\) means \(p_q(\beta^{\sigma}) \neq -p_q(\beta)\).

Building block values.

Knot Braid word Writhe \(w\) \(p_q(q_0)\)
\(0_1\) (unknot) \(e\) \(0\) \(0\)
\(3_1\) (trefoil) \(\sigma_1^3\) \(+3\) \(+3\)
\(3_1^{\sigma}\) \(\sigma_1^{-3}\) \(-3\) \(-3\)
\(4_1\) (figure-eight) \(\sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1} \sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1}\) \(0\) \(0\)
\(5_1\) (cinquefoil) \(\sigma_1^5\) \(+5\) \(+5\)
📄

Definition 4.22 ∀ stated (\(q\)-Angular momentum from the \(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)\) Casimir). \(\forall\)

The \(q\)-angular momentum of a particle is the \(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)\) Casimir eigenvalue of its knot representation.

Definition. Let \(K = \hat{\beta}\) be a knot/link with braid representative \(\beta \in B_n\). The \(q\)-angular momentum is defined by the \(q\)-Casimir operator \(C_q\) of \(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)\):

\[J_q^2(K) \;=\; [j]_q \, [j+1]_q \;=\; \frac{q^j - q^{-j}}{q - q^{-1}} \cdot \frac{q^{j+1} - q^{-(j+1)}}{q - q^{-1}}\]

where \(j\) is the spin quantum number determined by the Jones–Wenzl projector \(p_n\) acting on the \(n\)-strand braid: \(j = n/2\) for the highest-weight component.

At \(q = 1\): \(J_q^2 \to j(j+1)\), the standard Casimir.

The \(q\)-deformed angular momentum operators.

The generators \(J_+, J_-, J_z\) of \(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)\) satisfy:

\[[J_z, J_{\pm}] = \pm J_{\pm}, \qquad [J_+, J_-] = [2 J_z]_q \;=\; \frac{q^{2J_z} - q^{-2J_z}}{q - q^{-1}}\]

This differs from the classical \([J_+, J_-] = 2J_z\) by replacing \(2J_z\) with its \(q\)-number \([2J_z]_q\). The asymmetry at \(q \neq 1\) is directly connected to parity violation (parity violation): the raising and lowering operators are not related by a simple conjugation.

📄

Definition 4.23 ∀ stated (\(q\)-Deformed Energy). \(\forall\)

The \(q\)-energy of a particle knot \(K\) is the sum of three terms, each derived from the categorical triple \((\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)\) and the substrate parameter \(q\).

Definition. Let \(K = \hat{\beta}\) be a particle knot with braid representative \(\beta \in B_n\). The \(q\)-energy is:

\[\mathbf{E}_q(K) \;=\; \underbrace{J_q^2(K) \cdot \hbar_q}_{\text{rotational}} \;+\; \underbrace{p_q(\beta)^2 \cdot \hbar_q / (2\,[n]_q)}_{\text{translational}} \;+\; \underbrace{S_q(K)}_{\text{action (rest mass)}}\]

where:

  • \(J_q^2(K) = [j]_q [j+1]_q\) is the \(q\)-angular momentum (q-angular momentum),

  • \(p_q(\beta)\) is the \(q\)-momentum (writhe) (q-momentum),

  • \(S_q(K) = \mathrm{tr}_\tau(\rho(\beta))\) is the categorical action — the Markov trace of the braid in the Hecke algebra \(H_n(q)\),

  • \(\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}\) is the quantum Planck constant,

  • \([n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1})\) is the \(q\)-number.

The three terms.

  1. Rotational term \(J_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q\): The \(q\)-deformed rotational energy. For a spin-\(\frac{1}{2}\) particle at the substrate parameter \(q\): \([1/2]_q [3/2]_q \cdot \hbar_q \approx 0.818 \times 0.0991 = 0.0811\). This vanishes at \(q = 1\) (where \(\hbar_q \to 0\)).

  2. Translational term \(p_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q / (2[n]_q)\): The \(q\)-deformed kinetic energy from the writhe. The \([n]_q\) in the denominator is the \(q\)-deformed "number of strands" (inertia).

  3. Action term \(S_q(K)\): The categorical action \(S_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathscr{L}_q)\) evaluated on the knot. This is the rest mass energy — the net sum of all crossing energies in the braid word:

\[S_q(K) \;=\; \sum_{\text{crossings}} \mathbf{E}_\times(q) \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^2}\]

The action term dominates: for hadrons, \(S_q \sim 10^3\) MeV while the rotational and translational terms are \(O(\hbar_q) \sim 0.1\).

At rest (\(p_q = 0\), \(J_q = 0\)):

\[\mathbf{E}_q(K)\big|_{\text{rest}} \;=\; S_q(K) \;=\; \mathfrak{m}(K) c^2\]

recovering the topological mass formula.

Limits.

Limit \(\mathbf{E}_q\)
\(q = 1\) (classical) \(j(j+1) \cdot 0 + w^2 \cdot 0 + S_1 = S_1\)
\(q \to \infty\) (deep-quantum) \(J_q^2 \to q^{2j+1}, \; p_q \to w \cdot q, \; S_q \to \infty\)
Rest frame \(S_q(K)\) (mass)

Relation to crossing energy.

Each crossing in the braid word contributes energy \(\mathbf{E}_\times(q) = \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) = 0.1045\) (in units of the mass scale \(\mu_0\)). The total action is:

\[S_q(K) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{k} \mathbf{E}_\times^{(\epsilon_j)}(q)\]

where \(\epsilon_j = \pm 1\) is the crossing sign. For a positive crossing: \(\mathbf{E}_\times^{(+)} = q\). For a negative crossing: \(\mathbf{E}_\times^{(-)} = q^{-1}\). The asymmetry \(q \neq q^{-1}\) at the substrate parameter \(q\) means positive crossings carry more energy than negative ones — this is the energy signature of parity violation.

Exceptional Divisor and Vertex Operators

📄

Definition 4.24 ∀ stated (Exceptional divisor at \(p\)). \(\forall\) Let \((\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})\) be a QOU and let \(p \in M\) be a brane point with outward normal \(N(p) = p/\lvert p\rvert\) and positively-oriented tangent frame \((T_1, T_2)\). Set \(R = R_{\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})}\) and

\[O(p) \;=\; p + R\,N(p).\]

The exceptional divisor at \(p\) is the fibre of the state bundle \(\mathcal{S}\) at \(p\) — the \(\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\) fibre

\[\mathcal{S}_p \;=\; \pi^{-1}(p) \;=\; \bigl\{\, O(p) + R\bigl(\sin\phi\,(\cos\psi\,T_1 + \sin\psi\,T_2) - \cos\phi\,N\bigr) \;:\; \phi \in [0,\pi],\; \psi \in [0,2\pi) \,\bigr\},\]

where \(\pi\colon \widetilde{M} \to M\) is the blow-up map that replaces \(p\) with \(\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\).

📄

Definition 4.25 ∀ stated (Reeb bundle over the exceptional divisor). \(\forall\)

Let \((\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})\) be a QOU and let \(\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\) be the exceptional divisor at a brane point \(p\) (exceptional divisor). The Reeb bundle at \(p\) is the principal \(U(1)\)-bundle

\[\mathcal{R}_p \;=\; \bigl(\, S^3 \;\xrightarrow{\;\pi_H\;}\; \mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2, \;\xi_q\,\bigr),\]

where \(\pi_H\) is the Hopf fibration and \(\xi_q\) is the \(q\)-Reeb vector field generating the \(U(1)\) fibre action. The total space \(S^3\) carries the contact structure \(\ker\theta|_{S^3}\), and the substrate parameter \(q\) (substrate parameter) determines the connection \(1\)-form: the holonomy around a generator of \(\pi_1(S^1)\) is \(e^{2\pi i / [2]_q}\), where \([2]_q = q + q^{-1}\) is the quantum integer.

The Reeb bundle has three roles:

  1. Base \(\mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2\): parametrises the directions of departure from \(p\) — the internal colour space.

  2. Fibre \(U(1)\): the Reeb direction, generated by \(\xi_q\) — the one axis in the colour fibre where observations commute.

  3. Total space \(S^3\): the arena where braid words in \(B_n\) are evaluated via the Iwahori–Hecke algebra \(H_n(q)\).

📄

Definition 4.26 ∀ stated (Vertex operator on the exceptional divisor). \(\forall\)

Let \((\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})\) be a QOU, let \(\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\) be the exceptional divisor at a brane point \(p\) (exceptional divisor), and let \(\mathcal{R}_p\) be the Reeb bundle over \(\mathcal{S}_p\) (Reeb bundle).

The formal variable. In the standard VOA formalism, the formal variable \(z\) is an indeterminate in the ring of formal Laurent series. In the QOU it has a geometric realisation: \(z\) is the affine coordinate \(z = v_1/v_2\) on the projective line \(\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\) (projective line), which coincides with the contact affine coordinate \(Z = \alpha_H / \iota_\xi\,\alpha\) (contact affine chart) restricted to the fibre \(\mathcal{S}_p\). Algebraically, on the standard affine chart \(v_2 \neq 0\), \(z\) generates the coordinate ring \(\mathbb{C}[z]\).

The vertex operator algebra of the QOU at \(p\) is the triple \((V, Y, |0\rangle)\) defined as follows.

Graded state space. The \(\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\)-graded vector space is the brane tower:

\[V \;=\; \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} V_n, \qquad V_n \;=\; A_n \;=\; J^n(A_0),\]

where \(A_0 = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2))\) is the coordinate ring and \(J^n\) denotes the \(n\)-th jet prolongation (jet prolongation). The grading \(n\) is the conformal weight: the eigenvalue of the Reeb charge operator \(L_0 = \xi_q^{(0)}\) (the zero-mode of the \(q\)-Reeb vector field).

State-operator correspondence. The map

\[Y \colon V \;\longrightarrow\; (\mathrm{End}\,V)[\![z, z^{-1}]\!]\]

assigns to each state \(a \in V_n\) a vertex operator (a formal Laurent series in \(z\)):

\[Y(a, z) \;=\; \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} a_m\, z^{-m-1},\]

where the modes \(a_m \in \mathrm{End}\,V\) are defined by the \(R\)-matrix insertion:

\[a_m \;=\; \oint_{|z| = 1} Y(a, z)\, z^m\, \frac{dz}{2\pi i} \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^m \bigr),\]

with \(\check{R}_{(a)} = P \circ \mathcal{R}\) the braid operator (R-matrix braiding) applied to the state \(a\), and \(\mathrm{tr}_M\) the Markov trace (Jones–Markov trace). The contour integral is taken around the equator of \(\mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2\), i.e.
along a fibre of the Reeb bundle \(\mathcal{R}_p\).

Vacuum and translation.

\[|0\rangle = 1 \in A_0, \qquad T = L_{-1} = j \colon A_n \to A_{n+1},\]

where \(j\) is the jet prolongation map. The vacuum is the unknot (identity element of \(A_0\)), and the translation operator advances one level in the brane tower.

OPE as Skein resolution. When two insertion points \(z, w\) on \(\mathcal{S}_p\) collide, the operator product expansion

\[Y(a, z)\, Y(b, w) \;\sim\; \sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{Y(c_n, w)}{(z - w)^{n+1}}\]

has its leading singularity governed by the Hecke relation \((T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0\), which is the Skein relation

\[L_+ - L_- \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\, L_0.\]

The collision \(z \to w\) is two strands meeting on \(\mathcal{S}_p\); the resolution into \(L_+\), \(L_-\), \(L_0\) is the OPE decomposition into singular channels. The two eigenvalues \(q\) and \(-q^{-1}\) of \(T_i\) correspond to the symmetric (bosonic) and antisymmetric (fermionic) OPE channels respectively.

Vertex Factorisation and the Markov Trace

📄

Proposition 4.27 ∀ stated (Vertex operators factor through the exceptional divisor). \(\forall\)

Let \((\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})\) be a QOU with exceptional divisor \(\mathcal{S}_p = \pi^{-1}(p) \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\) at a brane point \(p\) (exceptional divisor), and let \(\mathcal{R}_p\) denote the Reeb bundle over \(\mathcal{S}_p\) (Reeb bundle). Then:

  1. Localisation. Every Hecke generator \(T_i \in H_n(q)\) acting on \(V^{\otimes n}\) factors through the fibre functor restricted to \(\mathcal{S}_p\). That is, the vertex operator \(T_i \colon V^{\otimes n} \to V^{\otimes n}\) is supported on \(\mathcal{S}_p\) and acts trivially on the base algebra \(A_0\).

  2. Confinement. Every Skein resolution \(L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0\) is evaluated within the Reeb bundle \(\mathcal{R}_p = S^3 \xrightarrow{\pi_H} \mathcal{S}_p\). The braid word \(\beta \in B_n\) representing the interaction is evaluated as a Markov trace in \(H_n(q)\) over \(\mathcal{R}_p\), and the result projects to \(A_0\) via the blow-down map \(\pi\).

  3. Completeness. Every interaction that changes quantum numbers at \(p\) — crossing change, pair creation, virtual exchange — is realised by a finite braid word in \(B_n\) whose Hecke image \(\rho(\beta) \in H_n(q)\) acts within \(\mathcal{R}_p\). No interaction requires data from outside the blow-up at \(p\).

Proof. (1) Localisation. The braiding of \(\mathbf{C}\) is given by the universal \(R\)-matrix \(\mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})^{\otimes 2}\) (R-matrix braiding), which acts on \(V^{\otimes n}\) by permuting tensor factors with a \(q\)-dependent phase. The Hecke generator is \(T_i = \tau_i \circ R_{i,i+1}\), where \(\tau_i\) is the transposition. Under the fibre functor \(\tau\), the representation \(V\) is a module over the coordinate ring \(\mathcal{O}(G_q)\), which is the structure sheaf of the exceptional divisor \(\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\) (the quantum flag variety of \(G_q\) at \(q\)). The \(R\)-matrix acts fibrewise: it permutes sections of \(V\) over \(\mathcal{S}_p\) without involving sections of the base algebra \(A_0\). Hence \(T_i\) is supported on \(\mathcal{S}_p\).

(2) Confinement. The Skein relation \(L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0\) is the image of the Hecke relation \((T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0\) under the Markov trace. Since \(T_i\) acts within \(\mathcal{S}_p\) (part 1), and the Markov trace is computed over the Reeb bundle \(\mathcal{R}_p\) (the \(U(1)\)-bundle whose connection is \(\xi_q\)), every Skein resolution is evaluated within \(\mathcal{R}_p\). The blow-down map \(\pi\colon \widetilde{M} \to M\) collapses \(\mathcal{S}_p\) to \(p\), projecting the resolved link invariant to the base level.

(3) Completeness. The Iwahori–Hecke algebra \(H_n(q)\) is generated by \(\{T_1, \ldots, T_{n-1}\}\) subject to the Hecke and braid relations. Every element of \(H_n(q)\) is a finite linear combination of products of these generators (braid action on tensor products). Since each generator acts within \(\mathcal{R}_p\), so does every finite product. Crossing changes, pair creation (R-II moves), and virtual exchange are all expressible as finite braid words in \(B_n\), whose Hecke images lie in \(H_n(q)\). No operation requires data from outside the blow-up. ◻

📄

Theorem 4.28 ∀ stated (Product factorization of the Markov trace). \(\forall\)

Let \(\beta \in B_n\) be a braid on \(n\) strands and let \(\rho(\beta) \in H_n(q)\) be its image under the Hecke quotient (Jones–Markov trace). After Hecke reduction, the element \(\rho(\beta)\) decomposes as a product of generator chains: for each generator \(\sigma_i\) (\(i = 0, \ldots, n-2\)), the crossings at \(\sigma_i\) reduce to a linear combination \(a_i \sigma_i + b_i\) with \(a_i, b_i \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]\).

Theorem. The Markov trace factors as a product over generators:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr) \;=\; \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i(q), \qquad \hat{V}_i(q) \;=\; z \cdot a_i + b_i,\]

where \(z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})\) is the Markov trace parameter. Each \(\hat{V}_i\) is the vertex volume at generator \(\sigma_i\) — the evaluation of the vertex operator \(Y(\sigma_i, z_i)\) at the \(i\)-th insertion point on the exceptional divisor (vertex operator).

Proof. The Markov trace processes the product by peeling generators from the right. At each step, \(\sigma_i\) is the rightmost (largest-index) generator in the remaining word, and the Markov property gives:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M(\cdots (a_i \sigma_i + b_i)) \;=\; (z \cdot a_i + b_i) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\cdots).\]

This works because:

  1. The chain at \(\sigma_i\) reduces to \(a_i \sigma_i + b_i\) (linear in \(\sigma_i\) and the identity).

  2. The Markov property \(\mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\) applies to the \(\sigma_i\) term.

  3. Generator \(\sigma_i\) is the rightmost active generator, so the Markov property applies directly.

  4. The remaining word involves only \(\sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{i-1}\), independent of \(\sigma_i\).

Applying this recursively from \(i = n-2\) down to \(i = 0\) gives the product formula. \(\square\)

Transfer Matrix and Topological Mass

📄

Definition 4.29 ∀ stated (Categorical transfer matrix). \(\forall\)

Let \(\mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \bowtie \mathcal{L}\) be a hadron at a brane point \(p\) (localized hadron), and let \(\mathcal{S}_p\) be the exceptional divisor at \(p\) (exceptional divisor).

Insertion points and the configuration space. The constituent knots \(K_i\) are simple objects in \(\mathbf{C}\), each factoring through a tensor power of \(V\) (knot factorization): \(K_i \hookrightarrow V^{\otimes 2j_i}\) via the PawLei embedding \(\iota_{j_i}\). The index \(i\) labels the constituent slot, not the knot type: several slots may carry the same simple object (e.g.\{} a proton has \(K_1 = K_2 = T_{2,3}\) for two up quarks). Each constituent has a vertex operator \(Y(K_i, z_i)\) inserted at a point \(z_i \in \mathcal{S}_p\). The \(n\)-tuple of insertion points is a point of the ordered configuration space

\[(z_1, \ldots, z_n) \;\in\; \mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p) \;=\; \bigl\{\,(z_1, \ldots, z_n) \in \mathcal{S}_p^{\,n} : z_i \neq z_j \text{ for } i \neq j\,\bigr\}.\]

The ordering matches the constituent list of \(\mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]\); identical knot types occupy distinct points on \(\mathcal{S}_p\). The constraint \(z_i \neq z_j\) is the source of OPE singularities \((z_i - z_j)^{-k}\) — it is what distinguishes two copies of the same knot within a single fibre.

These insertion points are not free after the first crossing: the link \(\mathcal{L}\) encoding the internal entanglement imposes algebraic relations among them. Concretely, each Hopf link between \(K_i\) and \(K_j\) constrains the pair \((z_i, z_j)\) via the OPE singularity — the Hecke relation \((T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0\) evaluated at the collision \(z_i \to z_j\).

Interaction filtration. The configuration space algebra carries a bi-filtration reflecting the two sources of structure in the Reeb flow (observation braid):

  1. Ascending (jet prolongation). The brane tower \(A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots\) (jet prolongation) grows with each Planck step. At step \(k\), the configuration space lifts to the \(k\)-th jet: insertion points acquire \(k\)-th order Taylor data, and knots with crossing number \(\leq k\) become encodable (jet-Planck steps). A configuration \(\mathcal{S}_0 = \sum_i (p_i, H_i)\) (bundle initial conditions) at any reference point in the affine chart may contain arbitrarily many constituents — including hadrons and photons (\(K = \varnothing\)) — each carrying only zeroth-order fibre data. The subsequent configurations \(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \ldots\) represent the forward light cone of interactions from that reference point; \(\mathcal{S}_{-1}, \mathcal{S}_{-2}, \ldots\) represent the backward light cone (undoing computation).

  2. Descending (Hecke relations). Within a given jet level, each crossing between slots \(i\) and \(j\) adds a Hecke relation \((T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0\) to an interaction ideal \(I_k \subset \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p))\). The ideals are nested: \(I_1 \subset I_2 \subset \cdots \subset I_m\), so relations from earlier crossings are never forgotten. The quotient \(\mathcal{O}_n / I_k\) shrinks monotonically — the insertion points become more constrained with each interaction.

The two directions are complementary: jet prolongation opens new degrees of freedom (higher-order Taylor coefficients, heavier knot types), while Hecke relations close them (correlating the insertion points that have interacted). The information-theoretic content of a hadron is the balance between these two: \(\eta_q\) \(q\)-bits of information per step (operational entropy) measures the net rate at which the ascending tower outruns the descending constraints.

Two levels of braiding operation. A braiding operation on \(\mathfrak{H}\) can be described at two levels:

  1. Constituent level. Operate on the insertion points \((z_1, \ldots, z_n)\) individually. A crossing between \(K_i\) and \(K_j\) applies the vertex operator \(Y(\sigma_k, z_k)\) at the relevant generator \(\sigma_k\), producing a transfer matrix \(T_{K_i, K_j}(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}])\) that acts on the Hecke chain at \(\sigma_k\).

  2. Composite level. Operate on the single insertion point \(z_H\) of the composite knot \(K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}}\) (the closure of the hadron braid word). The Markov trace of the full braid word factors as a product of vertex volumes (Markov trace product): \(\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q)\).

The categorical transfer matrix. A categorical transfer matrix for \(\mathfrak{H}_p\) is the equivalence class

\[\mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) \;=\; \bigl[\, T \,\bigr]_{\sim} \;\in\; \mathrm{End}\bigl(H_n(q)\bigr) \,\big/\, \sim\]

where \(T\) is any braiding operation on \(\mathfrak{H}\) (at either level) and the equivalence relation \(\sim\) identifies two operations \(T_1 \sim T_2\) whenever they produce the same vertex volume:

\[T_1 \sim T_2 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \hat{V}(T_1, q) = \hat{V}(T_2, q) \quad\text{as polynomials in } q.\]

This is well-defined because the vertex volume \(\hat{V}_i(q)\) depends only on the Markov trace of the Hecke-reduced element — not on the specific braid representative, the decomposition of \(\mathfrak{H}\) into constituents, or the path of braiding operations within \(\mathcal{S}_p\).

📄

Proposition 4.30 ∀ stated (Transfer matrix level independence). \(\forall\)

Let \(\mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \bowtie \mathcal{L}\) be a hadron with composite knot \(K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}}\). Let \(\mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}_p)\) be the categorical transfer matrix (categorical transfer matrix). Then:

  1. Constituent-composite agreement. The Markov trace computed from the constituent insertion points \((z_1, \ldots, z_n)\) and the Markov trace computed from the composite insertion point \(z_H\) yield the same Skein polynomial: \[\prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}(q) \;=\; \hat{V}^{\mathrm{comp}}(q) \;=\; P_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q).\]

  2. Path independence on \(\mathcal{S}_p\). Two braiding operations \(T_1, T_2\) on \(\mathfrak{H}\) that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations (isotopy equivalence) have the same categorical transfer matrix: \(\mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2)\). In particular, the specific sequence of crossing changes within the exceptional divisor \(\mathcal{S}_p\) does not affect the result — only the equivalence class of the final configuration matters.

  3. Well-definedness. The categorical transfer matrix \(\mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H})\) depends only on the isotopy class of the hadron \(\mathfrak{H}\) and the knot types \(K_i\) of its constituents. It is independent of:

    • the braid representative \(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}\),

    • the PawLei embedding \(\iota_{j_i}\) for each constituent,

    • the order of crossings evaluated within \(\mathcal{S}_p\).

Proof. (1) Constituent-composite agreement. The hadron \(\mathfrak{H} \hookrightarrow V^{\otimes 2(j_1 + \cdots + j_n)}\) embeds into a tensor power of \(V\) via the PawLei basis (knot factorization). The braid word \(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}} \in B_N\) (where \(N = 2(j_1 + \cdots + j_n)\)) acts on \(V^{\otimes N}\) through the Iwahori–Hecke algebra \(H_N(q)\).

At the constituent level, the crossings between \(K_i\) and \(K_j\) are grouped by generator index, and the Markov trace factors as \(\prod \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}\) (Markov trace product).

At the composite level, the same braid word \(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}\) has a unique Hecke reduction in \(H_N(q)\), and the Markov trace yields \(P_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}))\).

These are equal because the Markov trace product formula is an exact algebraic identity in \(H_N(q)\): the product \(\prod \hat{V}_i\) and the direct trace \(\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}))\) evaluate the same element of \(H_N(q)\). The factorization is not an approximation — it is a rewriting of the trace using the Markov property.

(2) Path independence on \(\mathcal{S}_p\). All braiding takes place within the exceptional divisor (vertex operators factor through \(\mathcal{S}_p\)). Two braiding operations \(T_1, T_2\) that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations have braid words \(\beta_1, \beta_2\) whose closures \(\hat{\beta}_1, \hat{\beta}_2\) are ambient-isotopic. By the link invariance of the Markov trace (Jones–Markov trace, property 3), \(\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_1)) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_2))\). Hence \(\hat{V}(T_1) = \hat{V}(T_2)\) and \(\mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2)\).

The specific sequence of crossings within \(\mathcal{S}_p\) does not matter: all that matters is the isotopy class of the resulting link. This is the content of "what happens in the exceptional divisor stays in the exceptional divisor" — the blow-down map \(\pi\) collapses \(\mathcal{S}_p\) to \(p\), erasing the internal history.

(3) Well-definedness. Independence from the braid representative is the link invariance of the Markov trace (part 2). Independence from the PawLei embedding follows from the \(q\)-Schur–Weyl duality: any two embeddings \(\iota, \iota'\) of \(V_{j_i}\) into \(V^{\otimes 2j_i}\) differ by an element of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra centralizer, which commutes with the Markov trace. Independence from the order of crossing evaluation follows from the right-to-left peeling argument in the Markov trace product (Markov trace product): the generators are peeled in decreasing order, and the result is independent of the order in which crossings at a fixed generator were originally applied. \(\square\) ◻

📄

Proposition 4.31 ∀ stated (Topological mass formula (Archimedean)). \(\forall\)

In the archimedean realisation (\(\mathbb{C}\)-quantum observable universe), the topological decomposition of mass (topological mass) specialises to a closed-form relationship between the mass of a particle, the hyperbolic volume of its associated knot, and the quantum Planck constant.

Proposition. Let \((\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)\) be the \(\mathbb{C}\)-quantum observable universe and let \(K\) be a hyperbolic knot whose complement carries the vortex topology of a stable particle, generated by \(N\) blow-ups along the brane tower. The descent involution \(\hat{\tau}_n\) (descent involution) induces the idempotent splitting \(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}\) (descent eigenspaces). Under the archimedean fibre functor, the descended trace evaluates to the holonomy \(\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\) and each transient trace to the quantum dilogarithm \(\Phi_q(z_i)\), giving the mass formula

\(\mathfrak{m}(K) \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{\,2}},\)

where \(\mathrm{Vol}(K)\) is the hyperbolic volume of \(S^3 \setminus K\) and \(\hbar_q = 1 - 1/q\) is the quantum Planck constant (quantum Planck constant) at the substrate parameter \(q\) (substrate parameter).

The derivation proceeds from the categorical decomposition (topological mass) via three identifications, each following from the archimedean bridge:

  1. The baseline holonomy term \(\lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0;\, \mathfrak{G}) \rVert\) evaluates to \(\mathrm{Vol}(K)\) via the Chern–Simons/volume correspondence for the hyperbolic knot complement.

  2. The exceptional divisor contributions \(\Phi_q(z_i)\) sum, after evaluation in the Briggs–Klein spectral coordinates, to \(\mathrm{Vol}(K) \cdot (1/\hbar_q^{\,2} - 1)\).

  3. Adding baseline and exceptional terms: \(\mathfrak{m} = \mathrm{Vol}(K) + \mathrm{Vol}(K)(1/\hbar_q^{\,2} - 1) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^{\,2}\).

Combined with the knot–particle dictionary identifying particles with specific knots (e.g.\{} the figure-eight knot \(4_1\) with the Higgs field), this formula determines the substrate parameter \(q\) from experimental mass ratios (see §6.10).

📄

Remark 4.32 ✗ no Lean (Skein Decomposition and Topological Mass Ratios).

This remark formalizes the refinement of the particle-topology mapping by shifting from torus knots to a framework grounded in hyperbolic volumes and Skein-deformed residues. By treating mass as the geometric resistance of the 1-jet bundle prolongation, the \(q\)-deformed Skein relation provides a rigorous "Mass Sum Rule" for composite hadronic states.

Braiding Relations and the Spectral Filter

📄

Proposition 4.33 ∀ stated (QU and QUO axioms as relations on Hecke generators). \(\forall\)

The vertex operator algebra \((V, Y, |0\rangle)\) (vertex operator) inherits every QU and QUO axiom as a relation on the Hecke generators \(T_1, \ldots, T_{n-1}\) of \(H_n(q)\). Below we list each axiom and its explicit translation into knot coordinates — braid words in \(T_i\), the affine coordinate \(z\) on \(\mathcal{S}_p\), the Markov trace \(\mathrm{tr}_M\), and cup/cap morphisms \(\cup\colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V\), \(\cap\colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1}\).

QU Axioms (Quantum Universe)

QU-1: Rigid braided monoidal structure

The braiding \(c_{V,V}\) acts on \(V^{\otimes n}\) via the Hecke representation \(\rho_n\colon B_n \to H_n(q)\) with \(T_i = \rho_n(\sigma_i)\). Rigidity and braiding are encoded by three families of relations:

(QU-1a) Hecke relation (quadratic):

\[T_i^2 \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\,T_i + 1 \qquad (1 \leq i \leq n-1).\]

Equivalently \((T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0\): the eigenvalues \(q\) (symmetric/bosonic channel) and \(-q^{-1}\) (antisymmetric/fermionic channel) correspond to the two OPE channels of the vertex algebra.

(QU-1b) Yang–Baxter relation (braid relation):

\[T_i\, T_{i+1}\, T_i \;=\; T_{i+1}\, T_i\, T_{i+1} \qquad (1 \leq i \leq n-2).\]

This is the hexagon axiom of the braided monoidal category, expressed in the Hecke basis.

(QU-1c) Far-commutativity:

\[T_i\, T_j \;=\; T_j\, T_i \qquad (|i - j| \geq 2).\]

Strands that do not share a crossing commute: locality of the vertex algebra OPE.

(QU-1d) Snake identities (rigidity):

The cup \(\cup\colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V\) and cap \(\cap\colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1}\) satisfy:

\[(\cap \otimes \mathrm{id}_V) \circ (\mathrm{id}_V \otimes \cup) \;=\; \mathrm{id}_V,\]

\[(\mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}} \otimes \cap) \circ (\cup \otimes \mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}}) \;=\; \mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}}.\]

In the graphical calculus these are the zig-zag straightenings. In knot coordinates, \(\cup\) and \(\cap\) are the Markov-trace cup/cap insertions: the contour-integral endpoints of \(Y(a, z)\) around the Reeb fibre.

QU-2: Frobenius–Hopf relations

The multiplication \(\mu\), comultiplication \(\Delta\), unit \(\eta\), counit \(\varepsilon\), antipode \(S\), and Frobenius form \(\int_A\) become operations on braid closures:

(QU-2a) Associativity:

\[\mu \circ (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) \;=\; \mu \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu) \colon A^{\otimes 3} \to A.\]

In knot coordinates: merging three strands is independent of grouping. For braid words \(\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3\):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( \rho(\beta_1 \cdot \beta_2) \cdot \rho(\beta_3) \bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( \rho(\beta_1) \cdot \rho(\beta_2 \cdot \beta_3) \bigr).\]

(QU-2b) Frobenius relation (sliding):

\[(\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta) \;=\; \Delta \circ \mu \;=\; (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu) \circ (\Delta \otimes \mathrm{id}).\]

In knot coordinates this is the saddle-point relation: a strand merge followed by a split equals a split followed by a merge. Graphically, this is the genus-\(0\) cobordism identity — a pair of pants composed either way gives the same surface.

(QU-2c) Non-degenerate Frobenius pairing (\(A \cong A^{\vee}\)):

The Frobenius pairing \(\int_A \circ \mu\colon A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1}\) is the Markov trace of the product:

\[\langle a, b \rangle_F \;=\; \int_A \mu(a \otimes b) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\hat{\beta}_a \cdot \hat{\beta}_b)\bigr),\]

where \(\hat{\beta}_a\) is the braid word representing state \(a\). Non-degeneracy means: for every nonzero braid word \(\beta\), there exists \(\beta'\) such that \(\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta \cdot \beta')) \neq 0\).

(QU-2d) Hopf (antipode) relation:

\[\mu \circ (S \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \;=\; \eta \circ \varepsilon \;=\; \mu \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes S) \circ \Delta.\]

In knot coordinates, the antipode \(S\) is the braid reversal (orientation reversal of all crossings):

\[S(T_i) \;=\; T_i^{-1} \;=\; T_i - (q - q^{-1}) \qquad\text{(from the Hecke relation)}.\]

The Hopf relation then reads: closing a braid word against its reverse yields the unknot (vacuum):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( \rho(\beta) \cdot \rho(\beta^{-1}) \bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(1) \;=\; J_{0_1}(q).\]

(QU-2e) Coassociativity and counit:

\[(\Delta \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \;=\; (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta) \circ \Delta, \qquad (\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \;=\; \mathrm{id} \;=\; (\mathrm{id} \otimes \varepsilon) \circ \Delta.\]

In knot coordinates: splitting a strand into three is independent of grouping, and the counit (trace evaluation at the unknot) acts as a unit for splitting.

QU-3: Fibre functor (Markov trace)

The fibre functor \(\tau\colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-Mod}\) realises as the Jones–Markov trace (Jones–Markov trace). Its defining relation on Hecke generators is:

(QU-3a) Markov property I (conjugation invariance):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(T_i \cdot w\bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(w \cdot T_i\bigr) \qquad \forall\, w \in H_n(q).\]

(QU-3b) Markov property II (stabilisation):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(w \cdot T_n^{\pm 1}\bigr) \;=\; \frac{1}{\delta}\;\mathrm{tr}_M(w) \qquad \text{for } w \in H_n(q) \subset H_{n+1}(q),\]

where \(\delta = -(q + q^{-1})\) is the writhe normalisation.

(QU-3c) Faithfulness:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr) = 0 \;\;\forall\, \beta \in B_n \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \rho(\beta) = 0 \;\text{in } H_n(q).\]

The fibre functor detects every nonzero morphism — equivalently, the Jones polynomial separates knots (modulo the open Jones conjecture for the full category; for torus knots this is a theorem ).

QU-4: Differential calculus (translation operator)

The Kähler differentials \(\Omega^1(A)\) in the vertex algebra are generated by the translation operator \(L_{-1} = j\) (jet prolongation):

(QU-4a) Translation relation:

\[[L_{-1},\, Y(a, z)] \;=\; \partial_z Y(a, z) \;=\; Y(L_{-1}\, a,\, z).\]

In Hecke generators, the mode expansion gives:

\[[L_{-1},\, a_m] \;=\; -m\, a_{m-1},\]

where \(a_m = \mathrm{tr}_M(\check{R}_{(a)}\, z^m)\) is the \(m\)-th mode of the vertex operator.

(QU-4b) Vacuum axiom:

\[Y(|0\rangle, z) \;=\; \mathrm{id}_V, \qquad L_{-1}\,|0\rangle \;=\; 0.\]

The unknot (\(|0\rangle = 1 \in A_0\)) produces the identity operator; translation annihilates the vacuum.

QUO Axioms (Observable Universe)

QUO-1: Non-degenerate integration

The Frobenius form \(\int_A\) induces \(A \cong A^{\vee}\). In knot coordinates this sharpens QU-2c:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta) \cdot \rho(\beta')\bigr) \;=\; 0 \;\;\forall\, \beta' \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \beta = \varnothing \;\text{(empty braid)}.\]

Equivalently, the Gram matrix \(G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{\beta_i} \cdot T_{\beta_j})\) over any normal-form basis \(\{T_{\beta_i}\}\) of \(H_n(q)\) is invertible.

QUO-2: Observability (\(\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0\))

There is no braid word invariant under the adjoint (conjugation) action. In Hecke generators:

\[T_i\, w\, T_i^{-1} \;=\; w \quad \forall\, i \quad\Longrightarrow\quad w \in R \cdot 1 \;\text{(scalar multiple of the identity)}.\]

Equivalently: the only braid word commuting with all generators is the identity. In the vertex algebra, this means there is no nontrivial state \(a \in V\) with \(Y(a, z) = \lambda\,\mathrm{id}\) for all \(z\) — every state produces a genuinely \(z\)-dependent operator.

QUO-3: Measurability (anomaly freedom)

The Chern classes \(c_1(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = c_2(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0\) translate via the fibre functor to:

(QUO-3a) First Chern class vanishing (\(c_1 = 0\)):

\[\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( T_i - T_i^{-1} \bigr) \;=\; 0.\]

This is the total writhe of the adjoint representation being zero — the adjoint bundle is orientable.

(QUO-3b) Second Chern class vanishing (\(c_2 = 0\)):

\[\sum_{i < j} \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( [T_i, T_j]\,[T_i, T_j]^{\dagger} \bigr) \;=\; 0,\]

where \([T_i, T_j] = T_i T_j - T_j T_i\) and \(\dagger\) is the anti-involution \(T_i^{\dagger} = T_i^{-1}\). This ensures no topological phases accumulate under transport around the adjoint bundle.

QUO-4: Categorical volume constraint

The exterior power \(\Lambda^2 V\) maps onto \(\mathbf{1}\) via a non-degenerate epimorphism \(\epsilon\) preserved by gauge automorphisms. The antisymmetriser in \(H_2(q)\) is:

\[\mathrm{Alt}_2 \;=\; \frac{1}{[2]_q}\bigl(\mathrm{id} - q^{-1}\, T_1\bigr), \qquad [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.\]

The volume constraint is:

\[\epsilon \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2 \;=\; \epsilon \colon V^{\otimes 2} \to \mathbf{1},\]

and for every gauge automorphism \(g \in \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau)\):

\[\epsilon \circ (\Lambda^2 g_V) \;=\; \epsilon.\]

In Hecke generators, this becomes: the antisymmetric contraction \(\epsilon\) satisfies

\[\epsilon\!\bigl(v \otimes w - q^{-1}\,(T_1 \cdot v \otimes w)\bigr) \;=\; [2]_q\;\epsilon(v \otimes w)\]

and is gauge-invariant, fixing the \(q\)-deformed volume element.

Cohomological Constraints in Knot Coordinates

The QU/QUO axioms imply a suite of cohomological constraints. Each translates into a relation on braid words, Hecke generators, and the Markov trace.

C-1: De Rham complex (\(d^2 = 0\) on horizontal forms)

The de Rham differential \(d\colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A)\) acts on modes via \(d(a_m\, z^{-m-1}\, dz) = a_{m-1}\, z^{-m}\, dz\). In knot coordinates, the nilpotence \(d^2 = 0\) on the horizontal subcomplex \(\Omega_H^k(A)\) reads:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl( \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^{m-2} \Bigr) \;-\; 2\,\mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl( \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^{m-1} \Bigr) \;+\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl( \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^{m} \Bigr) \;=\; 0\]

for all \(\xi\)-invariant states \(a\) (those annihilated by the weight operator: \([\xi, a] = 0\), i.e.\{} braid words in the centre of \(H_n(q)\)).

C-2: \(q\)-Deformed obstruction to nilpotence (\(d_q^2 \neq 0\))

The \(q\)-exterior derivative \(d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d\) satisfies (categorical \(d_q^2\)):

\[d_q^2\,\alpha \;=\; q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\;\omega_V \wedge_q [\xi,\, \alpha].\]

In knot coordinates, the weight operator \(\xi\) acts on modes as the writhe grading:

\[[\xi,\, a_m] \;=\; \mathrm{wr}(a)\, a_m, \qquad \mathrm{wr}(a) = \sum_i \mathrm{tr}_M(T_i - T_i^{-1}) \;\text{(writhe of $\hat{\beta}_a$)}.\]

The curvature 2-form \(\omega_V\) is the Hecke Casimir:

\[\omega_V \;=\; \sum_{i < j} (T_i\, T_j - T_j\, T_i)\, dz^i \wedge dz^j.\]

So \(d_q^2 = 0\) if and only if \(q = 1\) (classical limit) or \(\mathrm{wr}(\alpha) = 0\) (zero writhe, horizontal forms). For generic \(q \neq 1\) and non-horizontal \(\alpha\), \(d_q^2 \neq 0\): the \(q\)-deformed complex is not a cochain complex, and the obstruction is measured by writhe \(\times\) curvature.

C-3: Hodge star and Poincar’e duality

The categorical Hodge star (categorical Hodge star) \(\star\colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{n-k}(A)\) satisfies \(\star^2 = \mathrm{id}\). In knot coordinates, \(\star\) acts on modes via the antipode:

\[\star(a_m) \;=\; S(a_m)^* \;=\; (T_i^{-1})_m^* \qquad\text{where } (\cdot)^* \text{ is Frobenius conjugation.}\]

Poincar’e duality in knot coordinates: for all braid words \(\beta, \beta'\),

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( \rho(\beta) \cdot \star\,\rho(\beta') \bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( \rho(\beta) \cdot S(\rho(\beta'))^* \bigr) \;=\; \delta_{\beta,\, \beta'}\;\mathrm{vol},\]

where \(\mathrm{vol} = \int_A(\mathrm{vol}) = 1\) normalises the top form. The pairing is non-degenerate by QUO-1.

C-4: Euler characteristic constraint

The categorical Euler characteristic \(\chi(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A)\) is the rigidity trace. In knot coordinates this is the Jones polynomial of the unknot at strand count \(n\):

\[\chi(A) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}_{H_n(q)}) \;=\; [n]_q! \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{q^k - q^{-k}}{q - q^{-1}}.\]

Stability under jet prolongation (C-4a):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{id}_{J^1 H_n(q)}\bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{id}_{H_n(q)}\bigr).\]

The translation operator \(L_{-1}\) preserves the Euler characteristic: \(\chi(A_{n+1}) = \chi(A_n)\) for all brane levels.

Descartes constraint (C-4b): For the physical universe,

\[\chi(A) \;=\; -6 \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}) \;=\; -6.\]

This forces genus \(g = 4\) (Bring’s surface), bounding the embeddable torus knots to the 7 generators \(\mathcal{G}\).

C-5: Yekutieli obstruction classes

The quantum characteristic classes \(\kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B})\) (quantum characteristic classes) obstruct lifting from brane level \(n\) to \(n+1\). In knot variables, the obstruction is detected by the failure of Markov stabilisation at the jet level:

\[\kappa_n \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( \check{R}_{(n+1)} - L_{-1}\, \check{R}_{(n)} \bigr) \;\in\; H^2(\mathcal{S}_p,\, \mathcal{B}),\]

where \(\check{R}_{(n)}\) is the \(R\)-matrix at brane level \(n\). The class \(\kappa_n = 0\) iff the level-\((n+1)\) braiding is entirely determined by the level-\(n\) braiding via jet prolongation.

Perpetual obstruction (C-5a): When \(\chi(A) = -6\),

\[\kappa_n \;\neq\; 0 \qquad \forall\, n \geq 0.\]

In Hecke generators: at every brane level, there exist braid words \(\beta_{n+1} \in H_{n+1}(q)\) that cannot be written as \(L_{-1}(\beta_n)\) for any \(\beta_n \in H_n(q)\). The jet corrections and the base obstruction live in complementary subgroups, so cancellation is impossible.

C-6: Betti numbers and spectral sequence

The Betti numbers \(b_k = \dim H^k(\mathcal{S}_n, \mathbb{R})\) are controlled by the Leray–Serre spectral sequence. In knot variables, \(b_k\) counts linearly independent \(k\)-fold products of Hecke generators modulo the de Rham relation:

\[b_k(\mathcal{S}_n) \;=\; \dim_R\, \frac{ \ker\!\bigl(d\colon \Omega^k_{H_n(q)} \to \Omega^{k+1}_{H_n(q)}\bigr) }{ \mathrm{im}\!\bigl(d\colon \Omega^{k-1}_{H_n(q)} \to \Omega^k_{H_n(q)}\bigr) },\]

where \(\Omega^k_{H_n(q)}\) is the space of degree-\(k\) antisymmetric Hecke words:

\[\Omega^k_{H_n(q)} \;=\; \mathrm{span}\!\bigl\{ T_{i_1} T_{i_2} \cdots T_{i_k} \;\big|\; i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k \bigr\} \cdot \mathrm{Alt}_k,\]

with \(\mathrm{Alt}_k = \sum_{\pi \in S_k} \mathrm{sgn}(\pi)\, q^{-\ell(\pi)}\, T_\pi\) the \(q\)-antisymmetriser.

Euler check: \(\chi = \sum_k (-1)^k b_k = -6\) reproduces C-4b.

C-7: Instanton constraint (self-dual curvature)

The categorical instanton condition \(\star_q F_\nabla = F_\nabla\) (instanton on-shell) becomes a relation on the curvature 2-form in Hecke generators. The curvature \(F_\nabla = \nabla^2\) has components:

\[(F_\nabla)_{ij} \;=\; [T_i,\, T_j] \;+\; \sum_k f^k_{ij}\, T_k,\]

where \(f^k_{ij}\) are the structure constants of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra. The self-duality equation is:

\[\star_q\, (F_\nabla)_{ij} \;=\; (F_\nabla)_{ij} \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad S\!\bigl([T_i, T_j]\bigr)^* \;=\; [T_i, T_j].\]

That is, the curvature is invariant under the combined antipode-conjugation — it is self-adjoint in the Frobenius inner product.

Bogomolny bound (C-7a): The instanton number equals \(c_2(A)\):

\[\lVert F_\nabla \rVert^2 \;=\; \sum_{i < j} \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl( [T_i, T_j] \cdot [T_i, T_j]^{\dagger} \bigr) \;=\; c_2(A).\]

By QUO-3b this vanishes for the adjoint — the adjoint bundle is flat. For the fundamental representation, \(c_2(A)\) is the topological charge (knot crossing number modulo signs).

C-8: Hodge–Laplacian and harmonic braid words

The \(q\)-Laplacian \(\Delta_q = d_q\, \delta_q + \delta_q\, d_q\) (Hodge–Laplacian) is self-adjoint. In knot coordinates:

\[\Delta_q \;=\; q^{-2}\,\Delta \;+\; q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\bigl( \omega_V \wedge_q \iota_\xi \;+\; \iota_\xi\, \omega_V \wedge_q \bigr),\]

where \(\Delta = d\delta + \delta d\) is the undeformed Laplacian and \(\iota_\xi\) is contraction with the weight vector.

Harmonic states are braid words \(\beta\) satisfying \(\Delta_q\, \rho(\beta) = 0\). In Hecke generators:

\[\Delta_q\, T_\beta = 0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_q\,T_\beta = 0 \;\;\text{and}\;\; \delta_q\, T_\beta = 0.\]

The space \(\ker \Delta_q\) is the particle Hilbert space — its dimension equals the number of linearly independent knot-particles at each brane level.

C-9: Cohomological embedding (knot basis for \(H^*\))

The cohomology of the moduli surface \(\Sigma_g\) (cohomological embedding) admits a knot basis. In knot coordinates, each cohomology generator is a specific Hecke word:

\[H^*(\Sigma_4) \;=\; \mathrm{span}\!\bigl\{ 1,\; T_{(2,3)},\; T_{(2,5)},\; T_{(2,7)},\; T_{(3,5)},\; T_{(2,9)},\; T_{(3,4)},\; T_{(4_1)},\; T_{(4_1)}^*,\; \mathrm{vol} \bigr\},\]

where \(T_{(m,n)} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\sigma^{(m,n)}))\) denotes the Markov-trace evaluation of the torus knot braid word \(\sigma^{(m,n)} \in B_m\).

Hodge decomposition in Hecke generators:

\(H^p(\Sigma_4)\) dim Hecke generators
\(H^0\) \(1\) \(1\) (empty braid = photon)
\(H^{1,0}\) \(4\) \(T_{(2,3)},\; T_{(2,5)},\; T_{(2,7)},\; T_{(3,5)}\)
\(H^{0,1}\) \(4\) \(T_{(2,9)},\; T_{(3,4)},\; T_{(4_1)},\; T_{(4_1)}^*\)
\(H^2\) \(1\) \(\mathrm{vol} = \epsilon \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2\) (neutrino)

Completeness: the \(6 \times 5\) character matrix \(M_{ij} = \chi_{\lambda_j}(T_{(r_i, s_i)})\) over irreps \(\lambda \vdash r\) of \(H_2(q) \oplus H_3(q)\) has rank \(5\). Every knot observable on \(\Sigma_4\) is a linear combination of evaluations of the \(6\) torus-knot Hecke words.

C-10: \{}v{C}ech–Yekutieli descent cocycle

The cosimplicial crossed groupoid structure on the brane tower gives a \{}v{C}ech cocycle condition at each level. In knot variables, the twisted 2-cocycle reads:

\[d\!\bigl(g^{(n)}_{ijk}\bigr) \;=\; a^{(n)}_{ij} \cdot g^{(n)}_{ijk} \cdot \bigl(a^{(n)}_{jk}\bigr)^{-1},\]

where \(g^{(n)}_{ijk} \in H_n(q)\) is the transition braid word on triple overlaps and \(a^{(n)}_{ij}\) are 2-morphism braid words. In Hecke generators, the cocycle condition becomes:

\[T_{g_{ijk}} \cdot T_{g_{jkl}} \;=\; T_{a_{ij}} \cdot T_{g_{ikl}} \cdot T_{a_{kl}}^{-1} \qquad\text{(in $H_n(q)$)},\]

where \(T_g = \rho(g)\) denotes the Hecke image of a braid word. This is the gluing condition for locally defined braid words to patch into a global knot invariant.

Summary: complete presentation

The vertex operator algebra of a QUO is the quotient of the free algebra on generators \(\{T_i, \cup, \cap, L_{-1}, \mathrm{tr}_M, d, d_q, \star\}\) by the relations:

Structural relations (QU/QUO axioms):

Label Relation Axiom
QU-1a \(T_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})T_i + 1\) Hecke (braiding)
QU-1b \(T_i T_{i+1} T_i = T_{i+1} T_i T_{i+1}\) Yang–Baxter
QU-1c \(T_i T_j = T_j T_i\) (\(\lvert i-j\rvert \geq 2\)) Locality
QU-1d \((\cap \otimes 1)(1 \otimes \cup) = \mathrm{id}\) Rigidity
QU-2b \((\mu \otimes 1)(1 \otimes \Delta) = \Delta \circ \mu\) Frobenius
QU-2d \(\mu(S \otimes 1)\Delta = \eta\varepsilon\) Antipode
QU-3a \(\mathrm{tr}_M(T_i w) = \mathrm{tr}_M(w T_i)\) Markov I
QU-3b \(\mathrm{tr}_M(w T_n^{\pm 1}) = \delta^{-1}\mathrm{tr}_M(w)\) Markov II
QU-4a \([L_{-1}, a_m] = -m\,a_{m-1}\) Translation
QUO-1 \(\det G_{ij} \neq 0\) Non-degeneracy
QUO-2 \(T_i w T_i^{-1} = w\;\forall i \Rightarrow w \in R\) Observability
QUO-3a \(\sum_i \mathrm{tr}_M(T_i - T_i^{-1}) = 0\) \(c_1 = 0\)
QUO-3b \(\sum_{i<j} \mathrm{tr}_M([T_i,T_j][T_i,T_j]^{\dagger}) = 0\) \(c_2 = 0\)

Cohomological relations:

Label Relation Constraint
C-1 \(d^2 = 0\) on \(\ker[\xi, \cdot]\) De Rham nilpotence
C-2 \(d_q^2\alpha = q^{-1}(1-q^{-1})\omega_V\wedge_q[\xi,\alpha]\) \(q\)-obstruction
C-3 \(\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)\cdot S(\rho(\beta'))^*) = \delta_{\beta\beta'}\) Poincar’e duality
C-4a \(\chi(A_{n+1}) = \chi(A_n)\) Euler stability
C-4b \(\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}) = -6\) Descartes

C-6 \(b_k = \dim(\ker d / \mathrm{im}\, d)\) on \(\mathrm{Alt}_k \cdot H_n(q)\) Betti numbers

C-7a \(\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{tr}_M([T_i,T_j][T_i,T_j]^\dagger) = c_2(A)\) Bogomolny bound
C-8 \(\Delta_q T_\beta = 0 \Leftrightarrow d_q T_\beta = \delta_q T_\beta = 0\) Harmonic braids
C-9 \(\mathrm{rank}\, M_{ij} = 5\) on \(\Sigma_4\) Completeness
C-10 \(T_{g_{ijk}}T_{g_{jkl}} = T_{a_{ij}}T_{g_{ikl}}T_{a_{kl}}^{-1}\) \{}v{C}ech cocycle

These 26 relations (14 structural + 12 cohomological), together with the Hecke–Skein dictionary \(T \leftrightarrow L_+\), \(T^{-1} \leftrightarrow L_-\), \(1 \leftrightarrow L_0\), constitute a complete presentation of the QOU vertex algebra in knot coordinates — encoding both algebraic structure and cohomological topology in the single language of braid words and the Markov trace.

Proposition 4.34 ∀ stated (QU/QUO and cohomological relations on the jet bundle). \(\forall\)

Every relation in the QU/QUO presentation (vertex algebra relations) lifts to the jet bundle \(J^n(A) = A_n\) via the brane tower (recursive brane tower). The jet prolongation \(L_{-1}\colon A_n \to A_{n+1}\) promotes each level-\(n\) Iwahori–Hecke algebra \(H^{(n)}(q)\) to a level-\((n{+}1)\) Hecke algebra \(H^{(n+1)}(q)\), and the descent involution \(\hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}\) splits the level-\((n{+}1)\) relations into descended (inherited from level \(n\)) and transient (genuinely new at level \(n{+}1\)).

Write \(T_i^{(n)}\) for the Hecke generators at brane level \(n\), \(\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\) for the level-\(n\) Markov trace, and \(\check{R}^{(n)}\) for the \(R\)-matrix at level \(n\). The jet embedding is \(\ell_n\colon H^{(n)}(q) \hookrightarrow H^{(n+1)}(q)\) with \(\ell_n(T_i^{(n)}) = T_i^{(n+1)}\), and the descent is \(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}\colon H^{(n+1)}(q) \to H^{(n)}(q)\) with \(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}\).

I. Structural relations on \(J^n(A)\)

J-1: Hecke relations (level \(n\))

The Hecke generators at every brane level satisfy the same quadratic, braid, and locality relations:

(J-1a) \(\;T_i^{(n)\,2} \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\,T_i^{(n)} + 1\)

(J-1b) \(\;T_i^{(n)}\, T_{i+1}^{(n)}\, T_i^{(n)} \;=\; T_{i+1}^{(n)}\, T_i^{(n)}\, T_{i+1}^{(n)}\)

(J-1c) \(\;T_i^{(n)}\, T_j^{(n)} \;=\; T_j^{(n)}\, T_i^{(n)} \qquad (|i - j| \geq 2)\)

The substrate parameter \(q\) is the same at every level — this is the content of the Euler characteristic stability \(\chi(A_n) = \chi(A_0)\).

J-2: Jet-prolonged Frobenius–Hopf relations

The multiplication \(\mu_n\), comultiplication \(\Delta_n\), and antipode \(S_n\) on \(A_n\) are inherited from \(A_0\) by jet prolongation. The Frobenius relation lifts level by level:

(J-2a) Frobenius sliding at level \(n\):

\[(\mu_n \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta_n) \;=\; \Delta_n \circ \mu_n.\]

In knot coordinates:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl( \rho_n(\beta_1) \cdot \rho_n(\beta_2 \cdot \beta_3) \bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl( \rho_n(\beta_1 \cdot \beta_2) \cdot \rho_n(\beta_3) \bigr).\]

(J-2b) Antipode at level \(n\): \(\;S_n(T_i^{(n)}) = T_i^{(n)\,-1} = T_i^{(n)} - (q - q^{-1})\).

(J-2c) Level-\(n\) Frobenius pairing:

\[\langle a, b \rangle_n \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl( \rho_n(\hat{\beta}_a \cdot \hat{\beta}_b) \bigr).\]

Non-degeneracy: \(\det G^{(n)}_{ij} \neq 0\) at every brane level.

J-3: Markov trace at level \(n\)

(J-3a) Conjugation invariance:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(T_i^{(n)} \cdot w) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w \cdot T_i^{(n)}) \qquad \forall\, w \in H^{(n)}(q).\]

(J-3b) Stabilisation:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w \cdot T_m^{(n)\,\pm 1}) \;=\; \frac{1}{\delta}\;\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w), \qquad \delta = -(q + q^{-1}).\]

(J-3c) Inter-level compatibility (jet prolongation preserves the Markov trace):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}\!\bigl(\ell_n(w)\bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w) \qquad \forall\, w \in H^{(n)}(q).\]

This is the knot-variable form of Euler stability: the Jones polynomial of a knot is independent of brane level.

J-4: Translation operator between levels

(J-4a) Mode relation across levels:

\[[L_{-1},\, a_m^{(n)}] \;=\; -m\, a_{m-1}^{(n+1)},\]

where \(a_m^{(n)} = \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\check{R}^{(n)}_{(a)}\, z^m)\) is the \(m\)-th mode at level \(n\). The commutator maps level-\(n\) modes to level-\((n{+}1)\) modes — the translation operator is the inter-level ladder.

(J-4b) Vacuum stability across levels:

\[|0\rangle^{(n)} \;=\; \ell_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ \ell_0\,(|0\rangle) \;=\; 1 \in A_n.\]

The unknot embeds identically at every level.

J-5: Observability at level \(n\)

\[T_i^{(n)}\, w\, T_i^{(n)\,-1} = w \;\;\forall\, i \quad\Longrightarrow\quad w \in R \cdot 1 \;\;\text{in } H^{(n)}(q).\]

The vanishing of \(\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A_n))\) propagates from level \(0\) by the jet prolongation proof: any \(\mathrm{Ad}\)-invariant at level \(n{+}1\) projects to one at level \(n\), contradicting the base case.

J-6: Volume constraint at level \(n\)

\[\epsilon_n \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2^{(n)} \;=\; \epsilon_n, \qquad \epsilon_n \circ (\Lambda^2 g_V^{(n)}) = \epsilon_n.\]

The \(q\)-antisymmetriser \(\mathrm{Alt}_2^{(n)} = \frac{1}{[2]_q}(\mathrm{id} - q^{-1} T_1^{(n)})\) has the same form at every level (same \(q\)), so the volume constraint is level-independent.

II. Descent decomposition of relations

The descent involution \(\hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}\) is idempotent on \(H^{(n+1)}(q)\) and splits every relation into descended and transient parts.

D-1: Descended Hecke generators

\[\hat{\tau}_n(T_i^{(n+1)}) \;=\; \ell_n\!\bigl(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T_i^{(n+1)})\bigr) \;=\; \ell_n(T_i^{(n)}) \;=\; T_i^{(n+1)}.\]

For \(i \leq n-1\): the base Hecke generators are entirely descended — they are the same crossing at every level. The Hecke relation QU-1a is purely descended.

D-2: Transient generators

At level \(n{+}1\), the jet prolongation may produce new generators \(T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}\) in the transient complement \(\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1} = \ker\,\hat{\tau}_n\). These satisfy:

\[\hat{\tau}_n(T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}) \;=\; 0, \qquad \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}) \;=\; 0.\]

Transient generators have no pre-image at level \(n\). They still satisfy the Hecke relation (J-1a) at level \(n{+}1\) but their Markov traces are invisible at level \(n\):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl( \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}) \bigr) \;=\; 0.\]

D-3: Descent of the Frobenius relation

The Frobenius sliding relation (J-2a) splits as:

\[\Delta_n \circ \mu_n \;=\; \underbrace{ \hat{\tau}_n(\Delta_{n+1} \circ \mu_{n+1}) }_{\text{descended (from level $n$)}} \;+\; \underbrace{ (1 - \hat{\tau}_n)(\Delta_{n+1} \circ \mu_{n+1}) }_{\text{transient correction}}.\]

The transient correction encodes the jet curvature: the failure of the level-\((n{+}1)\) Frobenius relation to be entirely determined by level \(n\).

D-4: Bosonic vs fermionic modes

The descent eigenspaces (descent eigenspaces) separate modes by statistics:

  • Bosonic (longitudinal): \(w \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}_{n+1}\) satisfies \(\hat{\tau}_n(w) = w\). In knot coordinates: braid words whose Markov trace is fully determined at level \(n\):

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}(w) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(w)).\]

  • Fermionic (ladder): \(w \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1}\) satisfies \(\hat{\tau}_n(w) = 0\). In knot coordinates: braid words whose Markov trace vanishes when descended:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(w)) \;=\; 0.\]

Fermionic modes are the jet-created braid words with no analogue at the previous level.

III. Cohomological relations on \(J^n(A)\)

JC-1: De Rham complex at level \(n\)

\[d_n^2 \;=\; 0 \qquad\text{on } \Omega^k_H(A_n),\]

where \(\Omega^k_H(A_n)\) is the horizontal subcomplex at level \(n\) (braid words with zero writhe at level \(n\)).

JC-2: \(q\)-Obstruction at level \(n\)

\[d_{q,n}^2\,\alpha \;=\; q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\;\omega_V^{(n)} \wedge_q [\xi_n,\, \alpha],\]

where \(\omega_V^{(n)} = \sum_{i<j}(T_i^{(n)} T_j^{(n)} - T_j^{(n)} T_i^{(n)})\,dz^i \wedge dz^j\) is the level-\(n\) Hecke Casimir. Since \(q\) is level-independent, the obstruction to \(d_q^2 = 0\) has the same algebraic form at every level — but acts on a larger algebra.

JC-3: Euler characteristic stability

\[\chi(A_n) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathrm{id}_{H^{(n)}(q)}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(0)}(\mathrm{id}_{H^{(0)}(q)}) \;=\; \chi(A_0) \;=\; -6.\]

The rigidity trace of the identity is level-invariant. In Hecke generators: the quantum factorial \([n]_q!\) at the base strand count is preserved by jet prolongation.

JC-4: Yekutieli obstruction at level \(n\)

\[\kappa_n \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}\!\bigl( \check{R}^{(n+1)} - \ell_n(\check{R}^{(n)}) \bigr) \;\in\; H^2(\mathcal{S},\, \mathcal{B}).\]

In Hecke generators, this measures the transient part of the \(R\)-matrix:

\[\kappa_n \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}\!\bigl( (1 - \hat{\tau}_n)\, \check{R}^{(n+1)} \bigr).\]

The perpetual obstruction \(\kappa_n \neq 0\) means: at every level, the \(R\)-matrix has a nonzero transient component — braiding at level \(n{+}1\) is not entirely determined by level \(n\).

JC-5: Betti numbers across levels

\[b_k(A_{n+1}) \;=\; b_k^{\mathrm{desc}}(A_{n+1}) + b_k^{\mathrm{trans}}(A_{n+1}),\]

where

\[b_k^{\mathrm{desc}} \;=\; \dim \frac{ \ker(d_n) \cap \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}_{n+1} }{ \mathrm{im}(d_n) \cap \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}_{n+1} } \;=\; b_k(A_n)\]

and \(b_k^{\mathrm{trans}}\) counts genuinely new cohomology classes at level \(n{+}1\). The Leray–Serre spectral sequence for \(A_{n+1} \to A_n\) has \(E_2\)-page:

\[E_2^{p,r} \;=\; H^p\!\bigl(A_n,\; H^r(\Omega^1(A_n))\bigr) \;\Longrightarrow\; H^{p+r}(A_{n+1}),\]

with differentials controlled by \(\kappa_n\).

JC-6: Instanton constraint at level \(n\)

\[S_n\!\bigl([T_i^{(n)},\, T_j^{(n)}]\bigr)^* \;=\; [T_i^{(n)},\, T_j^{(n)}].\]

Self-duality of the curvature holds at every level by inheritance of the Frobenius-adjoint structure. The instanton number decomposes:

\[c_2(A_n) \;=\; c_2^{\mathrm{desc}}(A_n) + c_2^{\mathrm{trans}}(A_n),\]

where \(c_2^{\mathrm{desc}} = c_2(A_{n-1})\) is inherited and \(c_2^{\mathrm{trans}}\) is the topological charge of the transient sector.

JC-7: Harmonic braid words at level \(n\)

\[\Delta_{q,n}\, T_\beta^{(n)} = 0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_{q,n}\, T_\beta^{(n)} = 0 \;\;\text{and}\;\; \delta_{q,n}\, T_\beta^{(n)} = 0.\]

The harmonic space decomposes under descent:

\[\ker \Delta_{q,n+1} \;=\; \underbrace{ \ell_n(\ker \Delta_{q,n}) }_{\text{descended harmonics}} \;\oplus\; \underbrace{ \ker \Delta_{q,n+1} \cap \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1} }_{\text{new particles at level $n{+}1$}}.\]

Descended harmonics are the particles already present at level \(n\); transient harmonics are new particle states created by the jet prolongation.

JC-8: \{}v{C}ech cocycle at level \(n\)

\[T_{g^{(n)}_{ijk}} \cdot T_{g^{(n)}_{jkl}} \;=\; T_{a^{(n)}_{ij}} \cdot T_{g^{(n)}_{ikl}} \cdot T_{a^{(n)}_{kl}}^{-1} \qquad\text{in } H^{(n)}(q).\]

The cosimplicial structure links adjacent levels: the coface map \(\delta^i\) is jet prolongation \(\ell_n\), and the codegeneracy \(\sigma^j\) is descent \(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}\). The cosimplicial identities in knot coordinates:

\[\ell_n(T_{g^{(n)}_{ijk}}) \;=\; T_{g^{(n+1)}_{\delta^i(ijk)}}, \qquad \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T_{g^{(n+1)}_{ijk}}) \;=\; T_{g^{(n)}_{\sigma^j(ijk)}}.\]

JC-9: Global gluing (direct limit)

The direct limit \(\mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim\, H^{(n)}(q)\) is the infinite-level Iwahori–Hecke algebra. A braid word \(w_\infty \in \mathcal{A}_\infty\) is a compatible sequence \((w^{(0)}, w^{(1)}, w^{(2)}, \ldots)\) with \(\ell_n(w^{(n)}) = \hat{\tau}_n(w^{(n+1)})\) for all \(n\). The global Markov trace is:

\[\mathrm{tr}_M^{(\infty)}(w_\infty) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(0)}(w^{(0)}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w^{(n)}) \qquad\text{(level-independent)}.\]

All structural and cohomological relations hold in \(\mathcal{A}_\infty\). The global gluing condition ensures that locally defined braid words patch into a well-defined element of the direct limit.
